passages.original: Quibus verbis episcopi vestri nihil omnino ausi sunt respondere, quamvis diu frustra contenderitat, quod non iti Ecclesia prædicta sint fulura zizania, quia dixit Dominus, « Ager est hic mundus i (Matth. xm , 38) ; nec dixit, Ager eat Ecclesia. Nos autem mundum pro Ecclesiae significatione positum dicebamus, sicut etiam Cyprianus intellexit, quia per totum mundum futura præfigurabatur Ecclesia. Unde illi dicebant, mundum semper in malam significationem positum; et testimonia de Scripturis dabant, quia scriptum est, Si quis dilexerit mundum, non eat charitas Patris in illo (I Joan.
passages.english: To these words your bishops dared make no reply at all, although for a long time they argued in vain that it was not in the Church that tares were foretold to be, because the Lord said, "The field is this world" (Matt. 13:38), and did not say, "The field is the Church." We, however, said that "world" was used to signify the Church, as Cyprian also understood it, because the Church was prefigured as going to be throughout the whole world. passages.original: et cum eis in illa permansit, qui de hac re diversa senserunt : unde aut tunc Ecclesia perisse dicenda est, et non fuit jam ex qua nasceretur Donatus illorum ; aut si , quod verum est, permansit Ecclesia, non in ea contaminant mali bonos, sicut Cyprianus etiam judicavit, qui cum diversa sentientibus in eadem diversitate permansit. Ac per hoc isti se detestando sacrilegio schismatis induerunt, qai propter nescio quorum crimina non probata , etiamsi vera essent, nullo modo se ab unitate toto orbe dil'osa separare debuerunt.
passages.english: and he remained in it with those who held a different view on this matter. Hence either the Church must be said to have perished then, and there was no longer one from which their Donatus could be born; or, if the Church remained, which is the truth, the wicked do not defile the good within it, as Cyprian also judged, who remained in that same difference [of opinion] with those who thought differently. And for this reason these men have clothed themselves in the detestable sacrilege of schism, who on account of the unproven crimes of some people or other, even if they were true, ought in no way to have separated themselves from the unity spread throughout the whole world.
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence; the subject 'he' is Cyprian (from the preceding context). Scanning errors read as 'qui' (for 'qai') and 'diffusa' (for 'dil'osa').
